candidate.title: Digenome-Seq
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina Cas9 Digenome-seq schematic, interpreted at the level supported by the 2015 method abstract: genomic target-site illustrations, in vitro target-site digestion, whole-genome sequencing, and alignment-based cleavage-site detection. Deletion, Wild type and Insert are depicted sequence contexts within this one workflow. Multiplexed Digenome-seq, Cpf1 implementations and related off-target assays mentioned in the catalogue are outside the depicted scope. Library preparation is an unspecified interface within sequencing.

states.label: Genomic DNA containing candidate Cas9 cleavage sites
features: Left Genome line has a yellow highlighted region; the next line is labeled Cas9 target.

The central site illustrations are labeled Deletion, Wild type and Insert. The top blue line is shorter, the middle carries a target mark, and the bottom includes a magenta segment. Dotted continuations indicate genomic sequence outside the illustrated region.
These labels precede digestion. No operation that creates insertions or deletions, no separate sample allocation, and no pooling are depicted.

evidence.locator: Left Genome and Cas9 target drawings; three central DNA lines labeled Deletion, Wild type, Insert
Abstract: method definition and cleavage readout
evidence.quote: Here we present Digenome-seq, in vitro Cas9-digested whole-genome sequencing, to profile genome-wide Cas9 off-target effects in human cells. This in vitro digest yields sequence reads with the same 5' ends at cleavage sites that can be computationally identified.

evidence.locator: First arrow from Cas9 target to Deletion / Wild type / Insert; common arrow from these three site drawings into Target site digestion
evidence.rationale: The drawings compare three site contexts beneath one assay caption and along one set of stage arrows. There are no sample identifiers, branch connectors, split or pooling symbols. They are therefore represented together as a schematic collection of genomic site contexts, without asserting that the three contexts were independent samples or that the arrow creates indels. Their exact experimental identity remains unspecified.

states.label: In vitro Cas9-digested genomic DNA (digenome)
features: Cleavage generates genomic DNA fragment ends; recurrent cleavage at a site produces fragments sharing a 5′ end.

The Target site digestion drawing retains all three blue site-context lines and puts a yellow icon with blue outline at the middle target. Cleavage is indicated by the caption and subsequent read-end pattern; explicit strand-end chemistry is not drawn.
No chemical end-group formula, adapter, barcode, attachment or compartment is specified.

operations.label: Target site digestion
operations.description: Cas9 cleaves genomic DNA in vitro at susceptible sites, converting genomic substrates into a digenome containing cleavage-ended fragments. At the level of this schematic, the three labeled DNA drawings illustrate site contexts within that substrate; the arrows do not specify an indel-generation reaction or separate sample preparation.
operations.mechanism: RNA-guided Cas9 is the cleavage reagent, represented by the yellow/blue icon; single guide RNAs are identified in the primary abstract but are not separately drawn. Cleavage creates the DNA-end signal.
operations.information_effect: Sequence context and newly formed fragment termini physically associate each cleavage with a genomic position. Repeated cuts at a position create coincident fragment ends; no assertion of equal or complete cleavage of the three illustrated contexts is made.
